subject: Data sunset handshake: archive quarantine plan & log-hold carveouts
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Porter <elaine@nuvohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Data sunset handshake: archive quarantine plan & log-hold carveouts

Elaine —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Per our call, I wanted to put our proposed sunset/erase cadence in writing and surface a couple of carveouts Nuvo asked about so legal and ops can align. High level:

- Primary plan: user-data (PII) eligible for deletion will be deleted from primary store at 90 days after user erasure request, with a 30-day quarantine stage for recovery before final tombstone removal.
- Backups & snapshots: incremental backups retained for 180 days in our standard backup tier; snapshot tombstones are scheduled for purge on a 30/60/180 phased cadence depending on retention class.
- Logs & telemetry: standard application logs are maintained for 90 days; we can propose an exception window for security-forensic logs.
- Subprocessors: we will provide a matrix of subprocessors and geographic locations (attached).

Open asks for Nuvo:
1) Confirm whether the 90-day primary + 30-day quarantine is acceptable for consumer PII, or if you need 180-day preservation for HIPAA-adjacent records.
2) If your security team needs a longer forensic log window (we discussed 270 days), we’ll need a scoped DPA amendment + audit trail (see kI’s note below).
3) Any procurement or legal deadlines for signoff (Elaine, you mentioned year-end procurement review).

I’ve attached the proposed-erase-plan-v2.pdf for ops details and included Marissa and Karthik to handle the operational and DPA language. If it helps, we can route a one-page amendment through DocuSign once language is agreed.

Next steps: if Nuvo is ok with the 90+30 primary, we’ll prepare an ops runbook and a short DPA amendment that limits the log-hold carveout to explicit incident investigations with timeboxed retention and audit logs.

Best,

Jordan Blake
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Attachment: proposed-erase-plan-v2.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)
From: Elaine Porter <elaine@nuvohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nuvohealth.com>, CloudOps Lead <cloudops@nuvohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data sunset handshake: archive quarantine plan & log-hold carveouts

Jordan —

Thanks for the writeup and the PDF. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Legal/Compliance prefers 180-day retention for backups that may contain PHI-adjacent metadata; can you flag which backup classes contain that metadata?
- Procurement: we have a contract review on 12/15; if you can get any DPA amendment language to us before then it helps speed procurement.
- CloudOps: they want confirmation of which subprocessors actually see unencrypted backups.

We’re generally supportive of the 90+30 primary workflow for non-sensitive records, but we need a concrete proposal for the 180-day backup carveout and for an auditable log-hold process (who can request a hold, how it’s approved, and the retention ceiling).

Can Marissa and Karthik propose language we can circulate to legal/procurement?

—Elaine
Elaine Porter
Head of Security & Privacy | NuvoHealth
elaine@nuvohealth.com | +1 617-555-2110
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Porter <elaine@nuvohealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data sunset handshake: archive quarantine plan & log-hold carveouts

Thanks Elaine — appreciate the specifics. A couple operational notes and a short proposal below. Quoting your key asks for clarity:

> Legal/Compliance prefers 180-day retention for backups that may contain PHI-adjacent metadata; can you flag which backup classes contain that metadata?

- Flagging: our incremental backups (class: nearline-incr) and nightly full snapshots (class: snapshot-full) are the only classes where metadata may include pseudo-identifiers that Nuvo considers PHI-adjacent. I’ve annotated the attached subprocessor-matrix.csv to indicate which storage buckets and subprocessors have access.

> Procurement: we have a contract review on 12/15; if you can get any DPA amendment language to us before then it helps speed procurement.

- I’ve asked Karthik to draft a concise amendment below. If procurement can review a 1–2 paragraph amendment by 12/13 we can do a DocuSign loop before your 12/15 review.

> CloudOps: they want confirmation of which subprocessors actually see unencrypted backups.

- Short answer: none of our core backup subprocessors store backups unencrypted at rest. CloudStor (us-east-1) and ColdStore (eu-west-1) maintain encrypted-at-rest snapshots; keys are managed by Redwood KMS. We do have a limited restore play where decrypted data is mounted temporarily on a secured restore host (access is role-based and logged). See subprocessor-matrix.csv for per-bucket details.

Proposed operational carveouts (draft):
- Backups with PHI-adjacent metadata: retained up to 180 days; purged by automated job with a 7-day pre-purge notification to Nuvo contacts.
- Log-hold process: holds can be requested by Nuvo Security or Redwood Security via a formal ticket; holds expire after up to 270 days unless renewed with documented justification and executive approval (audit trail retained). Only scoped forensic logs (session traces, auth traces) are eligible; standard telemetry unaffected.
- Emergency extension: for legal holds related to subpoenas or litigation, Redwood will maintain evidence under legal hold until a certified lift is issued by both parties.

I attached the subprocessor-matrix.csv and annotated the relevant rows. If that looks right to you, Karthik can push a one-paragraph DPA amendment and we’ll prepare the DocuSign link.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Ops & Privacy | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: subprocessor-matrix.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Porter <elaine@nuvohealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 13:50:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data sunset handshake: archive quarantine plan & log-hold carveouts

Elaine / team —

Below is draft DPA amendment language we propose to cover the log-hold and backup carveouts. This is intentionally short so procurement can circulate quickly; we can expand into full exhibit language if requested.

DRAFT AMENDMENT (summary):
1) Backup retention carveout: For the avoidance of doubt, backups containing PHI-adjacent metadata will be retained by Redwood for a maximum of 180 days from creation, after which automated deletion will occur. Redwood will provide Nuvo with a pre-purge notification window of not less than 7 days and an export of retained object metadata on request.
2) Forensic log-hold carveout: Nuvo may request a scoped forensic log hold for incident investigation or regulatory inquiry. Such requests must be submitted in writing to Redwood Security and include justification; holds will be implemented within 48 hours and expire after 270 days unless renewed with written approval from Nuvo Legal and Redwood General Counsel. Redwood will log and disclose hold creation, extension, and release events to Nuvo for audit purposes.
3) Subprocessor transparency: Redwood will keep an up-to-date subprocessor list and promptly notify Nuvo of any changes affecting access to backups or logs; changes permitting access to unencrypted data will require prior written consent.

If Nuvo agrees to the above at a high level, Jordan — can you kick off the DocuSign with the attached one-paragraph amendment? I’ve attached dpa-amendment-draft.docx for procurement to review; small edits expected.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
